newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-BANNED WEAH APOLOGISES TO FIFA FOR "MOMENT OF CRAZINESS".
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BANNED WEAH APOLOGISES TO FIFA FOR "MOMENT OF CRAZINESS".

text.p: George Weah has apologised to FIFA for the "moment of craziness" which led to a six-match ban for butting Jorge Costa in a European Champions' League match.

AC Milan striker Weah, named on Thursday in an African squad to face Europe in an all-star match next month, said in a letter to FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter that he wanted to "extend his deepest regrets" over the butting incident.
Porto's Costa suffered a broken nose when he tangled with Weah in the players's tunnel after the match. He claimed Costa provoked him with racist slurs.

Weah, who had won FIFA's Fair Play Award just before the incident, said in his letter to soccer's governing body: "You have given me the greatest honour and because of a moment of craziness through provocation, I have caused you some embarassment."
He assured FIFA he would behave himself in the future.

Weah is one of 18 players in the All-Star squad of 20 who play for European clubs. The European side will not be able to call on Internazionale Milan, Marseille, Barcelona and Real Madrid players because of club commitments.
The match in Lisbon on January 29 is the first between all-star sides representing the the two continents.
